name: St. Andrew Kim Taegon Shrine
notes: Peaceful and photogenic. Korean architecture, and quiet enough to talk.

name: Victoria City Garden & Animal World
notes: Playful and interactive. Good for a sunset walk once the heat drops.

name: Krus sa Wawa & St. Martin of Tours Parish
notes: Historic and central. The grounds are open air and cost nothing to sit in.

name: Philippine Arena Stadium Grounds
notes: Grand and open air. Walk the perimeter; it is free and the light is good late.

name: The Stevia Farm
notes: Green and unhurried. Closes before dinner, so this is a daytime stop.

name: Bocaue Riverwalk Promenade
notes: Riverside and breezy. Best around 17:30 when the light comes off the water.

name: Turo Fireworks Hub
notes: Bright and festive. This is what the town is known for; go for the sparklers.

name: Cafe Galilea
notes: Cosy and aesthetic. Open late enough to be an after-dinner stop.

name: Kape at Kultura
notes: Warm and heritage-leaning. Opens early, so it works as a first stop.

name: Turo Night Food Park
notes: Bustling and casual. Evenings only, and cheap enough to graze across stalls.

name: Estero de Biñang Eats
notes: Comfort food, rustic room, friendly service.

name: La Casa Art & Coffee
notes: Creative and hands-on. Pottery and coffee; closed Monday and Tuesday.

name: Ciudad Dining Room
notes: Elegant and upscale. This is the anniversary room, not the weeknight one.

name: El Manzano Ancestral Home
notes: Vintage and intimate. Weekends only, and the house itself is half the visit.

name: Ligo-Ligo Riverside Retreat
notes: Private and tropical. Furthest out of the set, so budget for the trike.
